headline: Dell XPS 13 laptop is available starting today for $699, targeting budget market
summary: The low-cost laptop, announced last month, retails starting at $599 for students and $699 for other customers, positioning itself against Apple's MacBook Neo.
details: The Dell XPS 13, previously announced last month, is now officially available for purchase. It can be found on both virtual and physical store shelves, with pricing starting at $599 for students and $699 for general customers.

This budget-friendly laptop enters the market shortly after Apple unveiled its own entry-level device, the MacBook Neo. The MacBook Neo is primarily aimed at the education sector, targeting both teachers and students.

Apple has already secured a significant deal, supplying over 4,500 MacBook Neos to the Kansas City Public Schools. It remains to be seen if Dell's new XPS 13 will achieve similar success in this competitive segment.

headline_marked: [[Apple changes Hide My Email domain]], making it easier for sites to block anonymous sign-ups
headline: Apple changes Hide My Email domain, making it easier for sites to block anonymous sign-ups
summary: Apple is moving its anonymous Hide My Email addresses to a new @private.icloud.com domain. This change could allow websites and apps to more easily identify and block users employing the privacy feature.
details: Apple is set to alter its Hide My Email privacy feature, shifting anonymously generated email addresses to a new @private.icloud.com domain. This change, announced to developers, will make it simpler for apps and websites to detect and potentially block these private sign-ups.

Currently, Hide My Email, an iCloud+ feature, creates @icloud.com addresses that forward messages to a user's real inbox. These addresses are indistinguishable from regular Apple IDs, preserving user anonymity.

Apple stated that existing private addresses will continue to function without interruption. However, the company noted that app and email providers would need to update their filtering systems to ensure continued mail delivery to users of the feature.

The alteration has drawn criticism from Apple users on Reddit, who argue it will diminish the service's effectiveness. Apple has not yet responded to requests for comment regarding the reasons behind this change.

This move follows a previous incident where Apple reportedly provided real account information of a Hide My Email user to authorities, after the user allegedly sent a threatening email. This highlights ongoing tensions around online anonymity.
